CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain and right foot tingling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports being in his yard raking leaves yesterday. He felt fine initially but approximately two hours after returning inside, his back began tightening up and he developed pins and needles sensation in his right foot. He recalls a similar episode of back pain approximately three years ago that resolved after one day. He attempted treatment with ice and two ibuprofen tablets without improvement. He reports that a hot shower and sitting provide some relief. He denies regular physical activity. On examination, he reports pain with forward bending but denies pain when standing back up.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for tingling in right leg.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back pain approximately three years ago that resolved after one day.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient performed yard work yesterday. Denies regular physical activity.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Low back palpation reveals tenderness around L5. Pain elicited with forward flexion. No pain with extension. Dorsiflexion normal. Pulses equal in all extremities. Tingling noted in right leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain. Rest recommended. Meloxicam prescribed. Physical therapy prescribed for stretching and exercises. Patient to follow up in two weeks. MRI may be obtained if symptoms do not improve.
